messages:
Maria: FYI I ran the adaptive KV-slot-slimming experiment on the 32-GPU pool this morning with the new allocator headroom tweak. Summary: fewer OOMs but tail latency at 95% went up ~12% for seq=2048 workloads.
Akash: rough numbers? can you paste the perf counters / nvprof snippet?
Maria: paste below — took a short nsys capture during the spike window. Not pretty but shows frequent kernel fallbacks and more memcpy churn.
Maria: ```
# nsys snippet
Kernel: aten::attention_paged  avg_time=1.8ms  count=12000
Kernel: aten::attention_compact avg_time=2.4ms count=4300 fallback->compactless
Memcpy H2D avg=0.6ms count=900  H2D_bytes=1.1GB
KV cache evictions triggered=8200  prefix_hits dropped by 9%
```
Devon: hmm eviction up by 8-10% matches the slot slimming (we reduced reserved_workspaces by 15%). That should free more blocks but increase fragmentation.
Riley: did the allocator coalesce small free blocks? I remember the new coalesce window was disabled in that branch.
Maria: right — I disabled eager coalescing to avoid reclamation pauses. The tradeoff seems to be more small holes -> kernel chooses compactless path more often (worse perf).
Akash: can you share the allocator stats snapshot? free-list lengths, largest_free_run, avg_block_util?
Maria: here: ```
allocator_free_list_bins=64
avg_free_run_len=2
largest_free_run_blocks=11
block_size=256KB
block_reuse_hits=0.67
block_compactions=1300
```
Devon: block_size is 256KB still. For paged attention we might benefit from 128KB to pack more variable-length KV entries and reduce internal fragmentation. But watch compaction cost.
Akash: idea: adaptive block size per tenant/workload. Smaller blocks for short-seq-heavy workloads, otherwise keep 256KB. Could add heuristics based on recent median seq len and kv occupancy.
Riley: also we should try turning on lightweight coalescing: only coalesce runs when free_run_len>4 and evict_count since last_coalesce>200. That should avoid frequent pauses but still merge pathological holes.
Maria: agreed. I can run 3 arms: (A) revert reserved_workspaces (B) keep slim workspace + lightweight_coalesce (C) slim + 128KB min block. Run against replay of the customer 2048 workload and microbench NV.
InfraBot: canary deploy scheduled: eng-runtime/canary/kv-slot-slimming/2314567825 -> started
Akash: also kernel selection: are we scoring kernels based only on avg exec time? Maybe include fragmentation penalty: if fragmentation_ratio > 0.3 prefer fallback that is fragmentation-tolerant even if slightly slower avg.
Devon: yes, current kernel_selector uses {latency, memory_peak} scores. Add frag_penalty = max(0, frag_ratio - 0.25) * frag_weight. frag_weight tune = 0.8 initial.
Maria: noted. For the A/B, I'll collect: token throughput, 50/95/99 latency, allocator metrics, kernel fallback ratio, KV prefix hit rate, memcpy bytes.
Riley: for the compaction cost calc, we should instrument per-compaction CPU/GPU time (don't just count ops). I saw some compactions spiking 20ms which is bad for low-latency paths.
Maria: logging added. I'll push a tiny patch to capture compaction_duration_ms per op and log into the trace.
Akash: one more: could we reuse recently-evicted blocks for short-lived allocations to avoid zeroing or memcpy? a short-term LRU cache of freed blocks with a TTL could cut alloc cost.
Devon: yep — "warm free" pool. But we must invalidate on cross-tenant boundaries or pin metadata. Policy: warm_pool_max_age=2s, capacity=64 blocks per device. Might reduce H2D churn.
Maria: ok I'll include warm_free_pool as arm D if A/B/C are inconclusive. Running first two experiments now, ETA ~45m.
Akash: thanks. Anything I can monitor? add this dashboard query: kernel_fallback_ratio, kv_eviction_rate, allocator_frag_ratio, net H2D_bytes.
Maria: will post results when done. TL;DR so far: slimming reduces OOMs but exposes fragmentation -> kernel fallback and memcpy churn => latency regressions. Working plans: lightweight coalesce + kernel frag-aware scoring + optionally smaller blocks or warm-free pool.
Riley: thanks for running this — clear next steps. :thumbsup:
InfraBot: canary deploy completed: eng-runtime/canary/kv-slot-slimming/2314567843 -> success
Maria: quick follow-up after 2 runs: lightweight_coalesce reduced fallback ratio 40% -> 22% and 95p latency returned to +3% vs baseline. Pushing full experiment logs to the perf bucket.
